page.layout: One printed page (p. 126) with a running head at the top. Left margin holds notes beside the heading and the opening canon. The main text is one column. Below the canon, the paragraph continues onto the next page. The right edge shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: poniæ Imperator à Dairo, sponte se abdicante, declaratus novam Monarchiam condidit. De cujus factis, potentia & magnificentia stupenda plane & incredibilia referuntur. Ei ad nostra usq; tempora successerunt Fideryfamma Ongoschio & Chiongon.
main_text.head: II.Occi-dentalisOCCIDENTALIS, sive AMERICANA.
Canon.
main_text.p: America olim cognita fuitAmericani ex nostro orbe originem trahunt.

Certum est, jam antiquissimis tem-poribus Orbem illū Occidentalem à Phœnicibus, Carthaginiensibus, Hispa-nis aliisq; nationibus frequentatum habitatumque fuisse. Deinde omnis ipsius notitia periit, cùm excisâ à Ro-Phœnicibus Carthag. Hispanis &c.

page.notes: The first line begins mid-word ("poniæ"), the rest of "Japoniæ", so it is a fragment and marked cont="true". The notes "II." and "Occi-dentalis" stand beside the heading and are placed inside it, because no paragraph stands there. The "Occi-dentalis" margin label is partly abbreviated and uncertain, and it may read differently. The running head is read as "Regnum Japonicum." The word "Fideryfamma" was read from a small italic line and may be slightly off. No catchword or signature is printed. The ornamental capital "A" of AMERICANA is decorative.
